podcast.body: Released on May 18, 2010, this sixth album was a significant commercial breakthrough, earning five Grammy nominations and winning for Best Alternative Album and Best Artwork. Its cover, properly titled *Brothers* despite a longer, nonsensical version, is a tribute to a 1969 Howlin' Wolf album. The recording, which included one song produced by Danger Mouse, took place primarily at the Muscle Shoals Sound Studio in Alabama, a legendary location that presented significant challenges; its in-house gear was unusable after 30 years, and new digital equipment was fried by stray voltage. Despite this, the studio's acoustics and natural echo chambers were exceptional, emphasizing the bass on the record. The album's creation was marked by personal and band tensions, including Patrick Carney's contentious divorce. The physical CD was designed to change color when played: black to white in North America, white to black in Australia, and silver to black in Europe. "This record, which came out on May 18, 2010, was called Brothers."

podcast.body: Ten tracks from this album were recorded in the abandoned Muscle Shoals Sound Studio. The band brought their own equipment and worked amidst dust and cobwebs, demonstrating their "desperate" desire to absorb the lingering vibes of the historic space. "They worked through the dust and the cobwebs and recorded ten tracks from the Brothers album there."

The album was nominated for five Grammy Awards, winning Best Alternative Album and Best Artwork; the physical CD was designed to change color (black to white in US, white to black in Australia, silver to black in Europe) when heated by a CD player's laser.
